claim_under_test.id: F-13-15 (as stated in the Phase 5 claim text)
claim_under_test.title: srs/due/{deckId} issues N+1 queries — proven by query-stats delta
claim_under_test.claimed_state: Not fixed. 'every seeded deck is 10 words, so the cost is 27ms today and there is no large deck in real data to measure a before/after — fixing now would be an optimization without a number (P5).'
claim_under_test.claimed_root_cause: Per-word progress lookup inside a loop instead of one batched query for the deck's vocab ids.
claim_under_test.claimed_file_lines: SrsService.getDueWords lines 132-134 loop deckWords and call progressRepository.findByUserIdAndVocabularyId(userId, vocab.getId()) inside the loop

corrected_severity: NOT A FINDING (already fixed; the live endpoint issues zero per-word lookups)
reason: The claim describes a state of the code that no longer exists. At the audited commit (HEAD of audit-streak-review, working tree clean of any SrsService change relative to the fix) SrsService.getDueWords already performs ONE batched lookup via findByUserIdAndVocabularyIdIn and has done so under an explicit 'audit-v13 F-13-15' fix comment. The claim's own cited lines 132-134 are now that fix comment, not a loop calling the per-word repository method. Crucially, this is not merely a code-reading argument: the LIVE running backend (localhost:8080) was measured with sys.dm_exec_query_stats deltas around single calls and the per-word statement did NOT increment, while the batched statement incremented by exactly 1 per call.

live_evidence.target: GET /api/srs/due/10006 with a real student JWT (user@gmail.com), real DB rows
live_evidence.http: 200, median of 5 calls ~36ms (range 34.5-43.2ms) — consistent with the claimed 27ms order of magnitude, so the endpoint itself is real and reachable
live_evidence.deck_shape: deck_words for deck 10006 = 10 rows; all 10 decks in real data have exactly 10 words (SELECT deck_id, COUNT(*) FROM deck_words GROUP BY deck_id -> min 10 / max 10). The claim's 'every seeded deck is 10 words' is factually correct.
live_evidence.method: Two JPA statements were isolated by query_hash and execution_count in sys.dm_exec_query_stats, filtered to 'select uvp1_0%': (a) 0x7036764232593B0E = (@P0 bigint,@P1 bigint) = the PER-WORD lookup findByUserIdAndVocabularyId; (b) 0x1F1DD11708648468 = (@P0..@P10 bigint, 11 params) = the BATCHED lookup findByUserIdAndVocabularyIdIn (userId + 10 vocabIds).
live_evidence.control: Two consecutive reads 3s apart with NO api call: per-word 453 -> 453, batch 17 -> 17. Zero drift, so the counters are stable and deltas are attributable to the call.
live_evidence.delta_verdict: per-word lookup = +0 executions on every one of 4 isolated calls; batched lookup = +1 on every call. A 10-word deck calling the per-word method in a loop would have produced +10 per call. It produced 0. The N+1 is not present in the running build.
live_evidence.endpoint_attribution: Cross-check with two other endpoints over the same counter: srs/due/10006 moved batch 17->18; GET /api/srs/stats moved nothing; GET /api/decks moved nothing. The +1 batch delta is attributable specifically to srs/due/{deckId}.
live_evidence.no_residual_per_word_loading: Vocabulary loading was also checked (DeckWord.vocabulary is FetchType.LAZY): the vocabulary select hash 0xC54A3FD4E8F879E6 stayed at 60 before and after the call, and the deck_words select hash 0xDEEAB13533EEA857 moved 54->55 (one query for the deck, not one per word). No hidden per-word query remains.

source_evidence.working_tree: src/main/java/com/datn/engflow/service/SrsService.java lines 133-142 read: collect deckWords vocab ids -> findByUserIdAndVocabularyIdIn(userId, vocabIds) -> collect into Map<vocabId, progress> -> look up in the loop. There is no call to findByUserIdAndVocabularyId inside the loop.
source_evidence.fix_marker: The code carries an explicit comment: '// audit-v13 F-13-15: one batched progress lookup for the whole deck instead of a query per word.'
source_evidence.repository: UserVocabularyProgressRepository declares both findByUserIdAndVocabularyId (line 15) and findByUserIdAndVocabularyIdIn (line 25).
source_evidence.regression_test: src/test/java/com/datn/engflow/service/SrsDueWordsAuthzTest.java: dueWordsUsesOneBatchedProgressQueryNotOnePerWord verifies findByUserIdAndVocabularyIdIn called times(1) and findByUserIdAndVocabularyId never().
source_evidence.audit_records_agree: The audit's own artifacts record this as FIXED, not open: findings.md marks F-13-15 'FIXED'; evidence/f13-15-n1.json has status FIXED; REPORT.md line 127 lists F-13-15 as FIXED; performance.md section 3.4 is the historical 'before' note explicitly labelled 'KHÔNG tối ưu BÂY GIỜ' (not optimising now) with the intent recorded as a candidate, and round-2.md line 41 re-measures it as 'XÁC NHẬN — 0 per-word lookup sau fix'.

claim_provenance_note: The claim text is a verbatim snapshot of performance.md section 3.4, which was the Phase 5 BEFORE-fix observation. Read in isolation it asserts the N+1 is present and deliberately unfixed. That was true when measured, but it is stale as a statement about the system today: the fix landed as F-13-15 and is live. Re-asserting the 'before' note as a current MEDIUM finding is a drift error of exactly the class the repo has flagged before (see commit 93d44e5 'correct two stale claims').

severity_assessment.assessment: Not justified as a current finding. There is no live defect: the endpoint issues 1 batched progress query per call, measured directly. Even taken as a historical performance observation, the claim itself concedes it had no before/after number (10-word decks, 27ms) and therefore could not meet the bar the audit set for an optimization (P5). A stale 'before' note cannot carry MEDIUM against the current build.

steps: docker exec engflow-redis redis-cli --scan --pattern 'rate_limit:*' | xargs del  (flush buckets before each batch)
Baseline: python sweep/v8/sqlrun.py <query-stats query grouping by query_hash for 'select uvp1_0%'>
Re-read the same query-stats: per-word hash 0x7036764232593B0E stays flat; batch hash 0x1F1DD11708648468 increments by exactly 1
reproducibility.cleanup: No probe rows written. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_vocabulary_progress WHERE user_id=2 AND vocabulary_id<0 = 0. Read-only measurement; no DELETE batch was required.

answers_to_the_specific_questions.is_the_evidence_real_or_a_probe_artefact: The ORIGINAL before-fix measurement was plausibly real (10 per-word execs for a 10-word deck), but the claim as a CURRENT finding is an artefact of reading a stale 'before' note: it does not reproduce against the live build. Not a 429 artefact — buckets were flushed and calls returned 200; not a guard misread — the endpoint returned 200 with real data.
answers_to_the_specific_questions.is_severity_justified: No. Live system shows zero per-word lookups; MEDIUM is not supportable.
answers_to_the_specific_questions.is_this_correct_behaviour_rather_than_a_: The current implementation (one batched query + in-memory map) is correct behaviour and is the correct fix. The only defensible framing of the claim is as a historical record, already captured as FIXED in the audit's own files.
